By  Krisztian Sandor | Edited by  Nikhilesh De Oct 18, 2026, 7:28 p.m. EDT 2  min read Make preferred on Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email Make preferred on Wall Street street signs (Chenyu Guan/Unsplash) Summary Show Broadcom, Verizon and UnitedHealth are among nine companies objecting to having their shares traded on OKXICE’s planned tokenized-stock platform. The venue would use the SEC’s five-year Innovation Exemption to offer around-the-clock trading of blockchain-based shares backed one-for-one by underlying stock. Issuer resistance and uncertainty over the temporary regulatory framework could limit available stocks and discourage institutional investment in tokenized trading infrastructure. The SEC’s new framework for trading tokenized stocks is encountering resistance from some of the companies whose shares could trade, with Broadcom (AVGO), Verizon (VZ) and UnitedHealth (UNH) among the latest issuers to object. Eight newly disclosed objections appeared in an October 15 public notice from OKXICE, the joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) preparing to offer tokenized stock trading. Alongside Broadcom, Verizon and UnitedHealth, the notice names AppLovin (APP), Applied Digital (APLD), Rocket Lab (RKLB), CoreWeave (CRWV) and Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI). It lists nine objecting issuers in total, including AI chipmaker Cerebras Systems (CBRS), which formally opted out of being listed earlier. The update did not disclose why the companies objected or when they submitted their notices. Nasdaq (NDAQ) has separately said it would opt out of having its own shares tokenized under the framework, according to an FAQ on its website . A Nasdaq spokesperson told the Wall Street Journal that the company does not want its shares trading on a venue that does not display best prices in real time or report to the consolidated tape, which aggregates stock-market trading data. Nasdaq is not among the nine issuers named in OKXICE’s notice. Path to onchain stock trading OKXICE announced on October 5 that it had notified the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission of plans to launch the venue, initially targeting shares of 63 U.S.-listed companies. Former New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo, the venture’s co-chair, announced the move on X. The venue would operate under the SEC’s five-year “Innovation Exemption,” issued September 17, which allows qualifying platforms to trade tokenized U.S. stocks using automated market makers and liquidity pools. Tokenized stocks are blockchain-based representations of shares. OKXICE plans to operate around the clock using Uniswap v4 liquidity pools on OKX’s XLayer blockchain, with trades settled in stablecoins. Under the model described in its notice, underlying shares would be held one-for-one against outstanding tokens through a registered broker-dealer. Token holders must receive equivalent rights, including dividends and voting rights. Issuer doubts The issuer pushback echoes findings from TD Securities analysts led by Reid Noch, vice president of U.S. equity market structure. Conversations with dozens of issuers showed “little interest in tokenizing their shares outside a small group of crypto-adjacent companies,” the analysts wrote in a report shared with CoinDesk. Several issuers also approached the firm with significant concerns after discovering the framework, having been unaware of it when it was announced, the report said. TD Securities named the framework’s reliance on temporary exemptive relief, rather than permanent rules, as its largest hurdle. A future commission could reverse the approach, complicating the case for investing in infrastructure and discouraging institutions from integrating with venues even after they launch, the analysts said. That uncertainty is especially challenging when overseas platforms can continue offering synthetic stock products without assuming the operational requirements of the U.S. relief, they added. By  Jamie Crawley | Edited by  Oliver Knight Oct 20, 2026, 7:10 a.m. EDT 2  min read Make preferred on Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email Make preferred on (Shutterstock) Summary Show JPMorgan projects bitcoin will return 10% annually over the next decade in its base case, outpacing its forecasts for U.S. stocks, bonds and gold. The bank’s first range of long-term bitcoin forecasts spans from a 9.7% annual loss in its bear case to a 17% annual gain in its bull case. JPMorgan remains cautious about bitcoin, describing it as a speculative asset whose volatility and unstable correlations hinder its widespread inclusion in investment portfolios. Investment banking behemoth JPMorgan (JPM) expects bitcoin BTC $81,462.69 to outperform U.S. stocks, bonds and gold over the next 10 years. JPMorgan forecasted a base case of 10% annualized returns for bitcoin over the next 10 years in its 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions report on Tuesday. The bank also set a bear case of -9.7% and a bull case of 17%. The figure compared to projected 5.6%-6.6% growth in U.S. bonds, 7.5% and 7.7% in U.S. large and small-cap equities respectively and 5.5% in gold. The report marks the first time JPMorgan has put a range on bitcoin returns in its research. The New York based banking group has a complicated history with cryptocurrency, largely due to the association of CEO Jamie Dimon’s widely publicized views of bitcoin. Dimon famously described the world’s largest crypto as a “fraud” in 2017, a skeptical position he has reiterated with somewhat softer verbiage in recent years. JPMorgan maintained a cautious view of bitcoin in Tuesday’s report, saying its “volatility and unstable correlation to other asset classes…remain an obstacle to [its] widespread inclusion in portfolios.” Furthermore, the bank does not make a case for bitcoin as a portfolio diversifier, instead viewing it as a “speculative asset and a hedge against monetary easing,” according to comments by portfolio manager Dr Sheena Shah and head of digital asset strategy Dennis Cristallo. “It lacks a strategic role in portfolios other than as a bet on fiat currency expansion or future asset trading on blockchains,” they added. “BTC mostly trades like a high beta risk asset that tracks global money supply growth, but it is sometimes treated as ‘digital gold.’ Unstable correlations with other assets present a modeling hurdle. A further challenge is forecasting an asset whose fundamentals are not cash flows and whose economics may be as much about adoption, regulation and liquidity as technology.” Newsletters Crypto Daybook Americas - The latest moves in crypto markets, in context Market analysis for crypto traders and investors. By  Francisco Rodrigues | Edited by  Nikhilesh De Oct 18, 2026, 12:00 p.m. EDT 2  min read Make preferred on Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email Make preferred on Summary Show Latvia plans to allow residents to pay personal taxes with cryptocurrency as early as next year, according to PM adviser Didzis Dejus. Parliament passed a law taxing crypto withdrawals above deposits rather than individual trades, featuring a one-time declaration mechanism. The initiative aims to attract crypto firms and investors, supporting asset tokenization and positioning Latvia as a fast-moving fintech hub. Latvia could allow residents to pay personal taxes with cryptocurrency as early as next year, as part of a push to attract crypto firms and investors. The country’s Finance Ministry has agreed to the plan, though technical work with a payment provider remains, said Didzis Dejus, an adviser to the prime minister on strategic planning and the new economy. Asked whether Latvians would be able to pay taxes in crypto during the prime minister’s term, Dejus told CoinDesk at the UN:BLOCK Fintech conference in Riga that “I believe that will take place next year.” CoinDesk has reached out to Latvia’s Finance Ministry for comment but hasn’t heard back at the time of writing. The move would give crypto holders a way to use their assets to meet tax bills. It also builds on plans announced in May 2025 to enable crypto tax payments and the tokenization of other assets like real estate. “We are not afraid to be the fastest country,” Dejus said, describing efforts to attract crypto business beyond licensing. The proposal comes as Latvia changes how it taxes crypto investments. On Oct. 15, the country’s parliament passed legislation to tax withdrawals from crypto investment accounts once they exceed the amount deposited, rather than taxing each trade. The law also introduces a one-time declaration process. Holders can settle past tax obligations by paying 10% of their declared assets’ market value at the end of 2026. Declarations can be filed from April 1 to May 31, 2027, with the tax due by July 23. Dejus said the measure would help people who bought crypto years ago but lack records to prove what they paid. The payment plan’s timing could depend on the next government. Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs’ United List won the Oct. 3 parliamentary election, and is expected to be renominated, but still needs coalition partners. Latvia would not be the first government to accept crypto for taxes. Colorado started allowing crypto tax payments through PayPal in 2022, with funds converted into dollars. Dejus did not name Latvia’s payment provider or say which cryptocurrencies would qualify to pay taxes. Newsletters State of Crypto Examining the intersection of cryptocurrency and government. By  Shaurya Malwa | Edited by  Sheldon Reback Updated  Oct 19, 2026, 7:25 a.m. EDT Published Oct 19, 2026, 5:15 a.m. EDT 2  min read Make preferred on Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email Make preferred on Bitcoin mining offshoot loses Microsoft AI deal as power delay stretches into 2030s. (Winston Chen/Unsplash) Summary Show Microsoft abandoned a planned Nscale AI data center in the U.K. after the local grid operator said sufficient power might not be available until the early-to-mid 2030s. The facility was expected to supply 50 megawatts of computing capacity to Microsoft’s Azure cloud by early 2027, using 23,040 Nvidia chips. The setback highlights the power and financing challenges facing bitcoin miners expanding into AI infrastructure, as U.K. data center grid-connection requests total about 73 gigawatts. Technology giant Microsoft MSFT walked away from a planned U.K. AI data center run by Nscale, a company spun out of bitcoin BTC $81,522.53 mining, after the local grid operator said it may not be able to power the site for a decade. The site in Loughton, Essex, about 6 miles northeast of London, was meant to house 23,040 Nvidia chips and supply 50 megawatts of computing to Microsoft’s Azure cloud by early 2027, according to the Guardian , which followed initial reporting by the Financial Times. UK Power Networks, which runs the local grid, told Nscale there may not be enough capacity until the early-to-mid 2030s. Nscale announced the project last year alongside Microsoft, Nvidia NVDA and OpenAI. When the Guardian visited in February, the site was still a working scaffolding yard. Nscale has since cleared the location and is looking at other ways to bring in power. It said its other Microsoft contracts remain in place. Nscale grew out of Arkon Energy, which built sites for bitcoin mining. Its founder, Josh Payne, took that experience in locking down land and power and turned it into a business selling computing to AI companies. Much of the listed mining industry is now running that playbook. When CoinDesk looked at the industry shift in March , public miners had announced more than $70 billion in AI and high-performance computing contracts. They had also cut their combined bitcoin holdings by more than 15,000 BTC from their peaks, partly by selling coins to pay for the buildout. Mining was already getting squeezed then. The report put the average listed miner’s cash cost to produce one bitcoin near $80,000 in the fourth quarter of 2025, and bitcoin was trading around $70,000 by March. AI contracts pay steadily for years, but the sites are far more expensive to build. Estimates suggest an AI-ready facility runs $8 million to $15 million per megawatt, compared with roughly $700,000 to $1 million for bitcoin mining, and AI customers expect the servers to stay up around the clock. The money also takes time to show up. In its latest mining report , fund manager CoinShares counted more than 4 gigawatts of AI capacity under contract across the miners it tracks, with only about 550 megawatts actually billing customers. Contract backlogs topped $100 billion, while annualized AI revenue stood at just over $1 billion. Unless Nscale finds its own power or gets the grid to move a lot faster, the site it just cleared could sit idle for years. Meanwhile, Britain’s grid queue is long. Energy regulator Ofgem says data center projects have requested connections totaling about 73 gigawatts of demand. It is weighing tougher rules because some applicants may never build, which holds up projects that are ready to go. Bitcoin traded near $82,500, while Nasdaq futures gained more than 1% and major Asian stock indexes advanced after last week’s technology-led losses. China’s economy grew 4.5% from a year earlier in the third quarter, while retail sales exceeded expectations and signaled stronger domestic demand. Financial markets are a sea of green on Monday as upbeat China data and lower oil prices revive investor risk appetite. Starting with bitcoin. The leading cryptocurrency by market value was trading around $83,000 during early European hours, up 1% since midnight UTC and 1.60% over the past 24 hours. Nasdaq futures rose more than 1%, alongside a 1.8% gain in Japan’s Nikkei and a 0.6% advance in South Korea’s Kospi. Those markets took a beating last week, led by losses in AI-related shares. Elsewhere, Chinese stocks were up 0.3%. Gold was largely unchanged near $4,180, while the Dollar Index held near Friday’s lows, below 102. China’s gross domestic product (GDP) grew 4.5% year on year in the third quarter, according to data from the National Bureau of Statistics released Monday. That was faster than the second quarter’s 4.3% pace. Other data also pointed to stronger domestic demand in the world’s second-largest economy. Retail sales of consumer goods rose 1.1%, more than double the 0.5% increase expected and up from 0.4% the previous month. China is the world’s factory, its second-largest economy and a major importer of industrial commodities. Strong economic data from the country therefore tends to encourage risk-taking across financial markets. The rebound is also consistent with the VIX’s historical tendency to normalize after Friday spikes, a pattern that has often coincided with steadier equity markets. Oil prices fell on both sides of the Atlantic, reversing some of last week’s gains. Reuters attributed the decline to expectations that President Donald Trump’s Russia waiver would boost supply. Still, geopolitical risks in the Middle East persist. A sustained decline in oil could ease inflation fears, clearing the way for the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates. Bitcoin BTC $81,466.90 dropped about 1.1% over the last 24 hours, ether ETH $2,382.12 fell 1.7% and the broader CoinDesk 20 ( CD20 ) Index lost roughly 1.6%, pulled lower by declines in Asian stocks and the rising price of oil. Further weakness in equities could damp demand, analysts at QCP Capital wrote in a note published Monday. That may be on the cards. Both Nasdaq 100 futures and S&P 500 futures are lower, with companies including Coinbase Global COIN and Galaxy Digital GLXY falling in pre-market trading. “Broader equity deleveraging dynamics could transmit to cryptocurrency markets and potentially threaten the $80,000 support level if sustained,” the analsysts wrote. For the time being, the bitcoin price remains above that level after demand for the largest cryptocurrency picked up on Monday, as illustrated by the spot U.S. bitcoin ETFs. The funds posted their biggest net inflows in a month and BlackRock’s IBIT recorded its largest inflows in over a year. Monday’s fund flows offer encouragement for bulls, though demand remains concentrated. The ETFs attracted roughly $527 million in net flows, with BlackRock’s taking in $665 million while those from Fidelity and Grayscale recorded withdrawals. The ether ETFs lost $103.3 million, their fourth consecutive day of outflows, showing bitcoin-specific demand rather than demand for the wider crypto sector. Conversely, the analysts added, a continued Treasury rally could support risk assets, particularly alongside falling real yields and a weaker dollar. Even so, the macro backdrop leaves little room for complacency. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield is around 5.13%, while Brent crude is trading near $110 a barrel, keeping energy-driven inflation risks a headwind that could worsen if the geopolitical backdrop doesn’t improve. The Federal Reserve is widely expected to hold interest rates steady next week, though a 25 basis-point increase is being priced in for next month on prediction markets , leaving little reassurance for investors worried about tightening conditions. By  Oliver Knight , Omkar Godbole | Edited by  Sheldon Reback Oct 19, 2026, 6:26 a.m. EDT 3  min read Make preferred on Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email Make preferred on DeFi leads the way (CoinDesk data) Summary Show Bitcoin traded around $82,500, up about 0.4% since midnight UTC, extending a rebound from Sunday’s dip to roughly $80,700. The CoinDesk 80 gained 0.9%, triple the CoinDesk 5’s 0.e5% rise, with all six members of the DeFi index higher and arbitrum adding 6.7%. Nasdaq 100 futures rose more than 1% and Asian stocks advanced after China’s third-quarter GDP growth beat expectations and oil prices eased. Bitcoin BTC $81,516.37 is trading around $82,500, up around 0.5% since midnight UTC, extending a bounce from Sunday’s dip to roughly $80,700 and comfortably above Thursday’s brief break below $80,000. Altcoins outpaced the largest cryptocurrency, with ether ETH $2,386.68 adding 0.75% to near $2,430 and the CoinDesk 80 (CD80) gaining 0.9%, triple the 0.35% rise in the bitcoin-heavy CoinDesk 5 (CD5). DeFi led the CoinDesk benchmarks with a 0.81% gain, with all six members of the DFX sector index higher. The rebound follows a rough week for U.S. tech. The Nasdaq fell 4.5% in its worst weekly decline since June as worries over AI spending and debt hit stocks such as CoreWeave (CRWV), which fell 25%. On Monday, Nasdaq 100 futures advanced more than 1% alongside gains in Asian stocks after China’s third-quarter GDP growth of 4.5% beat expectations and oil prices eased, with earnings from Meta Platforms META and Tesla TSLA due this week. Derivatives positioning Volume jumps, positioning doesn't: Total 24-hour crypto futures volume rose 51% to $146 billion, while open interest (OI) edged up just 1.25% to $141 billion as traders churned through more contracts without adding much net exposure. Liquidations were $329 million, little changed from a day earlier, and the taker long-short volume ratio is balanced, so neither side is forcing the other out. Majors rally with more leverage than spot buying: BTC, ETH, SOL and XRP all gained, and their notional OI grew faster than their prices in a sign that fresh capital is entering the contracts. Annualized perpetual funding is positive on all four, so longs are paying to hold. The 24-hour OI-adjusted cumulative volume delta (CVD) is flat to negative, though, meaning aggressive selling at least matched aggressive buying. The gains look position-led, and that makes them more fragile. DOGE, UNI and crude oil perps see positions unwind: OI fell in all three despite flat-to-negative price action. Traders are closing positions and pulling capital out, not adding to bets on the downside. ADA's bounce meets bearish positioning: ADA rose almost 1% in 24 hours, yet its annualized perp funding is -8%, the only negative print among the majors. Shorts are paying to stay short, and CVD is negative too. If the bounce continues, that crowded short side could become a source of buying. Crypto volatility gauges stay calm as the VIX spikes: Bitcoin's and ether's 30-day implied volatility indexes, BVIV and EVIV, still signal calm, even as Wall Street's equivalent, VIX, surged on Friday. VIX history points to a likely normalization on Monday. Bitcoin put-buyers dominate Deribit : The five most traded options on Deribit over the past 24 hours were all bitcoin puts at strikes below the current market price. Traders use puts to hedge long exposure against spot declines, so some are insuring gains. Ether flows look mixed. Token talk Arbitrum ARB $0.1892 , an Ethereum layer-2 token, rose 6.7% to about $0.20, with the rally stemming from the Arbitrum Foundation’s Stablecoin Growth Program , announced on Thursday. The program sets aside 2 million ARB for the first 10 teams to hold $10 million in USDG, a dollar-pegged stablecoin issued by Paxos Digital Singapore. ARB has risen by 16.45% since the announcement. Pump.fun PUMP $0.004426 , the token of the Solana memecoin launchpad, jumped 7.6%, recouping part of a weekend slide that took it to about $0.0039 on Sunday. While there was no news catalyst for the move, 24-hour trading volume doubled to $215 million. DeFi tokens advanced across the board, with uniswap (UNI) up 3.2% to around $7.42, while lido LDO $0.3923 and ethena (ENA) rose by 2.5% and 1.6% respectively as the sector recovers from last month’s Clarity Act delay and shrinking yields . Celestia (TIA) gave back 3.9% to about 61 cents after Friday’s 16% jump, while starknet STRK $0.05656 slipped 1.0% to 6 cents. STRK’s market value has fallen about a quarter since Friday morning, according to CoinDesk data. The larger cryptocurrencies were mostly higher, with solana (SOL) rising 1.6% to about $106, XRP gaining 0.6% and BNB adding 0.36%. Cardano ADA $0.2164 slipped 0.15% and hedera HBAR $0.08260 fell 0.83%. The “Altcoin Season” index is at 56/100, tumbling from last week’s high of 63/100, the 2026 record. By  Jesse Hamilton | Edited by  Stephen Alpher Oct 19, 2026, 12:47 p.m. EDT 2  min read Make preferred on Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email Make preferred on CME Group hasn't shown it's being hurt by the new U.S. perpetual futures policies, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission contends. (CoinDesk) Summary Show The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission is seeking to cast doubt on CME Group's legal challenge to its new perps policy. The CFTC filed a brief in court arguing that the derivatives giant hasn't shown it's being harmed by the government's new push into perpetual futures, and without harm, it doesn't have legal standing. The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission threw open the doors for perpetual futures in the U.S. in May, approving the first bitcoin perp from Kalshi and suggesting that it was open for business on ensuring a domestic surge in such contracts. But the CME Group objected in court , and the CFTC has responded in court that the derivatives giant has no right to get in the way. "Allegations of increased competition, without any plausible inference of an imminent financial injury," don't give CME the legal standing to challenge the CFTC's actions, the agency said in a brief filed on Friday, noting that volume in crypto futures at the CME has actually risen since its policy shift. Perp contracts had soared overseas, becoming a major form of transaction in crypto derivatives, and the CFTC's move sought to clarify how the market could get rolling in the U.S. The agency — in response to President Donald Trump's aggressive crypto agenda that included bringing perps into domestic trading — said it'll regulate the products on a case-by-case basis as futures . Perps allow traders to speculate on the future price of an asset with a typically leveraged position, and the contracts don't come with a built-in expiration. But CME, which operates the leading global venues for derivatives trading, has insisted the contracts are not futures, because they have no end date. They're really swaps, the company's argument would have it, which would come with an entirely different regulatory approach. Spokespeople for CME didn't immediately respond to a request for comment on the CFTC's latest filing. The CFTC first asked a federal judge to dismiss CME's case last month, and this latest filing details its argument against the company's legal standing. "CME must plausibly allege an actual or imminent increase in competition," the CFTC argued. "CME has not even done that." The agency argued that CME has been telling investors that it hasn't heard of a demand for perps and that they aren't substitutes for the futures it's offering. "CME cannot have it one way with the court and another way with the investing public on earnings calls," the CFTC contended in its brief. Jaret Seiberg, a policy analyst at TD Cowen, argued in a Monday client note that CME may still have the edge, in both its standing as a competitor and its argument that perps may be appropriately treated as swaps. However, the clock is ticking on the new market. Newsletters State of Crypto Examining the intersection of cryptocurrency and government. By  Shaurya Malwa | Edited by  Omkar Godbole Oct 19, 2026, 8:16 a.m. EDT 2  min read Make preferred on Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email Make preferred on Charles Hoskinson (CoinDesk archives) Summary Show Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson said he is personally developing a new programming language with Input Output Global engineer Lucas Rosa. The language would combine transaction intents, proof-carrying data and Groth16 proofs to help applications execute user requests and efficiently verify that conditions were met. Hoskinson has not disclosed the language’s name, released public code or announced when developers will be able to use it. Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson is writing a new programming language for his blockchain. He says it will be the first to combine what a user wants a transaction to do with cryptographic proof that the rules were followed. “I’m actually personally developing a programming language for Cardano,” Hoskinson wrote on X on Sunday, adding that he’s working on it with Lucas Rosa, a software engineer at Input Output Global who co-created Aiken, one of Cardano’s main smart contract languages. That’s not something most founders do once their network is this big. Hoskinson runs a company full of engineers and is still choosing to write the tool future Cardano apps could be built on himself. The language would support three tools: transaction intents, proof-carrying data and Groth16 proofs. An intent lets a user say what they want done and leave the steps to the app. A trader could ask to swap one token for another only if the final price meets set conditions, without spelling out how to get there. Proof-carrying data attaches cryptographic evidence to a piece of information, showing it follows certain rules. Another app can check that evidence without redoing every calculation behind it. Groth16 is a widely used proof system that produces tiny proofs computers can check quickly. Those proofs can show a condition was met without revealing the private data used to meet it. Together, they could let developers build apps that coordinate trades, check complicated conditions, and pass verified information between services, with Cardano checking a small proof at the end. Cardano developers already write smart contracts in Plutus, which is built on the programming language Haskell, and in Aiken. Midnight, the privacy-focused blockchain built by Hoskinson’s company Input Output Global, has its own language, Compact, for apps that handle confidential data. Meanwhile, Hoskinson hasn’t shared the new language’s name, any public code, or a date when developers can start using it. Crypto lending vaults have attracted more than $10 billion in deposits, as investors seek returns on their digital assets, according to the Financial Times . Deposits have risen from $4 billion at the start of last year, highlighting growing demand for strategies that put stablecoins and other tokens to work. Vaults operate through smart contracts on decentralized finance platforms. Each has a “curator”, effectively an investment manager, who selects lending strategies, sets risk limits and collects fees. Returns typically range from 3% to 10%, although riskier strategies can generate as much as 20% or more. The appeal comes with considerable risks. Loans can be backed by illiquid tokens, crypto-backed stablecoins or tokenized private credit, leaving depositors exposed if collateral loses value or becomes difficult to sell. Automatic liquidations can intensify market declines, while hacks, coding errors and flawed pricing mechanisms create additional vulnerabilities. Publicly accessible smart contracts offer transparency, but investors may focus on headline yields without understanding the underlying exposure. Fintech companies, digital asset treasury businesses and hedge funds are among the main depositors, according to the article. Bitcoin backed lender Two Prime are among the firms entering the market. In September, it rolled out a bitcoin lending vault on Pareto targeting annual yields of 1.5% to 2% through institutional lending. The vault accepts wrapped bitcoin, requires a minimum deposit of 5 WBTC and has roughly $10 million of Two Prime’s capital committed to absorb initial losses. Regulators are examining whether existing rules should apply. The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has raised questions about vaults holding securities, while European regulators have proposed oversight of intermediaries providing access to DeFi. By  Shaurya Malwa | Edited by  Omkar Godbole Updated  Oct 19, 2026, 2:58 a.m. EDT Published Oct 19, 2026, 1:23 a.m. EDT 3  min read Make preferred on Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email Make preferred on Zcash developers plan a fix to keep ZEC swaps private from future quantum computers. (Shutterstock) Summary Show Zakura wants to assign a separate viewing key to every ZEC swap made through NEAR Intents, limiting the payment history that a future quantum computer could uncover from a publicly posted refund address. The proposal would keep spending keys with users while using private information retrieval to help wallets locate refunds without revealing which addresses they are checking. Zakura says compatible software wallets could adopt the open-source feature within weeks, before Zcash developers’ January target for quantum-resistant payments. Zcash is designed to make crypto payments private. But a future quantum computer could theoretically exploit a small gap in NEAR Intents, a cross-chain swapping service, to connect a user’s private ZEC transactions to their wallet, undermining that privacy. Fortunately, the team behind Zakura, a newer version of the software that runs the Zcash network, is taking steps to address that. In a new engineering post , it proposed giving every ZEC swap made through NEAR Intents its own private key. The change would close a gap that a future quantum computer could use to piece together a user’s payment history. NEAR Intents is a service that lets users swap tokens across different blockchains. When someone swaps private ZEC for USDC through it, the service posts one of their private Zcash addresses on NEAR’s public chain, so it knows where to send back any unused ZEC. That address goes up as soon as the deposit lands and stays there even if the swap goes through and no refund is ever needed. Such addresses give away no information on today’s computers. Each Zcash address carries a public key built from the wallet’s viewing key, the secret a wallet uses to spot payments sent to it, using one-way elliptic-curve math similar to what protects bitcoin and ether wallets. Ordinary computers can’t run that math in reverse, but a large enough quantum computer running Shor’s algorithm, a method published in 1994 for exactly that job, could theoretically work backward from the address to the key. That’s the real threat hanging over Satoshi-era bitcoin , whose public keys already sit onchain for anyone to copy. Last week, Google said its Willow quantum chip had produced near-perfect versions of one of the components such an attack would burn through, a step toward a machine powerful enough to try it. Quantum computers capable of that are still likely years away (and no one has a firm timeline for when one could be built), but it’s a problem developers across the industry are rushing to solve. One key for every swap Zcash’s architecture creates its own problem. A Zcash wallet can generate many addresses that look unrelated, but they usually share one viewing key. An attacker who cracks that key from a single published address could link every payment the account ever received and read the amounts and the private notes, or memos, attached to them. Spending takes a separate key, so the funds themselves would stay safe. Zakura’s fix gives each swap its own viewing key and leaves the spending key with the user’s main account. An attacker who someday cracks a refund address on NEAR would see only the payments tied to that one swap. How one key per swap keeps Zcash payments private. (Shaurya Malwa/CoinDesk) The design also deals with a practical snag. A wallet that has made hundreds of swaps would end up with hundreds of keys, and restoring it from a backup would mean scanning the entire Zcash chain with every one of them. Zakura’s answer is a database the wallet can query privately using a technique called private information retrieval. The wallet asks where its refunds landed, and the database answers without learning which addresses the wallet asked about. As such, no quantum computer has been demonstrated that can recover these keys. Zakura says wallets built on its open-source libraries, including Vizor, could add the feature in the coming weeks, with hardware wallets following once their firmware supports it. That would put the fix in users’ hands ahead of the January target Zcash developers set earlier this month for quantum-resistant payments. Wall Street's fear gauge, the VIX index, spiked on Friday as stocks dropped. History says Friday panics usually fade on Monday. Seasonality and calm bitcoin markets suggest the same. By  Omkar Godbole | Edited by  Nikhilesh De Updated  Oct 18, 2026, 7:24 p.m. EDT Published Oct 18, 2026, 12:33 p.m. EDT 3  min read Make preferred on Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email Make preferred on Friday VIX scares usually subside on Monday. (TradingView/CoinDesk) Summary Show Wall Street’s fear gauge, VIX, surged 21.5% Friday as stocks fell. Traders are betting the fear index will stay elevated through November. Historical data suggests Friday VIX spikes typically ease on Monday. Bitcoin remains above $80,000 over the weekend, with its own fear gauge, BVIV, pinned in familiar ranges, showing no signs of market stress. Wall Street's fear gauge, the VIX index, ripped higher on Friday as stocks tanked on AI and geopolitical worries. Bitcoin BTC $81,466.90 traded in a choppy manner as well. Traders are betting the fear gauge keeps climbing. However, if VIX history and bitcoin’s steady weekend price action are any guide, the panic could subside just as quickly on Monday. First, a quick primer. Cboe’s VIX measures how much traders expect the S&P 500, the blue-chip stock index, to swing over the next four weeks. It's derived from options prices. When people get nervous, they buy options, which are contracts used to hedge against price swings. That pushes the VIX up. Bitcoin BTC $81,466.90 , meanwhile, is the only macro asset thats trades over the weekend. As such, swings in bitcoin over the weekend are often seen as lead indicators of how traditional markets may open on Monday. Friday’s VIX surge On Friday, the VIX jumped 21.5% to 19.99 as the S&P 500 fell by 1.09%. That's VIX’s biggest one-day rise since June 5, when the S&P 500 suffered its worst day in months, according to data source TradingView. Traders are betting the VIX stays high through November. CNBC reports that traders bought 9,200 of the Nov. 18, 20-strike calls for $1.7 million. Traders also bought 12,500 of the Nov. 18, 23-strike calls for $1.1 million. The bet is that the VIX closes above 23 by the third week of November. That sentiment is consistent with the present macro developments. AI stocks have been hit hard in the week gone by. The cost of default insurance on AI-related firms has hit record highs . Geopolitics is pushing oil higher too. On Saturday, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz. The Russia-Ukraine front looks like it's heating up as well. VIX history favors a Monday reset Big Friday jumps in the VIX usually don't last, according to historical data. CoinDesk's analysis of the data finds the VIX has jumped 20% or more on a Friday 32 times since January 1990, not counting the latest one. The next Monday, it fell 25 times and rose just seven. In other words, investors slept over the Friday panic over the weekend and things normalized on Monday. The typical  Monday move was a drop of 4.5%. A month later, the VIX was lower in 25 of the 32 cases, and the median drop was 16%. Oil prices fell on both sides of the Atlantic, reversing some of last week’s gains. Reuters attributed the decline to expectations that President Donald Trump’s Russia waiver would boost supply. Still, geopolitical risks in the Middle East persist. A sustained decline in oil could ease inflation fears, clearing the way for the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates. As of this writing, the central bank is expected to keep its benchmark borrowing cost unchanged in the 4.75% to 5% range this month. It raised rates by 25 basis points last month. 07:37 UTC: Updates BTC’s price in the meta title and text. South Korea’s Kospi fell 3.73% to its lowest close since April 7 as SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics declined, with renewed AI spending worries weighing on chipmakers’ shares. Bitcoin BTC $81,462.69 slipped to around $81,400 on Tuesday, down 0.5% since midnight UTC, even after U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds attracted $526.6 million on Monday , their largest daily inflow in nearly a month. Asian stocks set the tone, with South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index falling 3.73% to its lowest close since April 7 as SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics declined with renewed worries over AI spending weighing on chipmakers’ shares. Nasdaq 100 futures fell 0.31%. Altcoin losses were broadly in line with bitcoin. Ether ETH $2,385.82 fell 0.9% to near $2,385 and the CoinDesk 80 (CD80) lost 0.34%, compared with a 0.33% drop for the bitcoin-heavy CoinDesk 5 (CD5). DeFi gave back Monday’s lead, with the sector index (DFX) dropping 1.2%, the weakest of the CoinDesk benchmarks. Brent crude is near $110 a barrel as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia keep supply risks in view. Roughly 70 S&P 500 companies report earnings this week, with General Motors before the bell and United Airlines after the close. Derivatives positioning Bitcoin open interest on Coinalyze fell to $27.4 billion, down 0.6% over 24 hours, while the aggregated funding rate was roughly 8.8% annualized. Ether’s funding of about 3.9% annualized suggests a bullish bias among traders. Longs hold around 55% of bitcoin positions , Coinalyze data shows, with a long/short ratio of 1.24. Binance’s top traders show a similar tilt, with a BTC-USDT position ratio of 1.78 on CoinGlass. Puts outtraded calls by more than two to one on Deribit over 24 hours, with the Oct. 30 $80,000 put the busiest contract. Out-of-the-money puts also cost more than equivalent calls, by 2.5 to 4 volatility points across expiries, a bearish skew that shows traders paying for downside protection even as open interest leans toward calls at $90,000-$100,000 for Oct. 30. CoinGlass shows $155.1 million of liquidations over 24 hours, down 54.7% from the previous day, with longs about 69% of the total on CoinMarketCap’s tally. Bitcoin and ether each saw around $30 million on Coinalyze, together about half of the $120.6 million it tracked. Token talk Celestia (TIA) rose 2.2% to around 63 cents, the biggest gainer on the CoinDesk 100 Index (CD100), adding to a gain of about 42% over the month. The run has coincided with Celestia’s Oct. 1 benchmark showing its Fibre scaling system averaging 3.07 terabits per second. At the same time, options exchange Derive chose Celestia for data availability in its V3 release. The next test is an unlock of 5.58 million TIA on Oct. 31, according to Tokenomist. Sandbox SAND $0.05742 led the CD100 lower with a 4.5% drop to about 6 cents, giving back part of a gain of about 30% over the month. That rally began after South Korean crypto exchanges Upbit, Bithumb and Coinone lifted trading cautions imposed in August following a bridge exploit. Layer-2 tokens were among the weakest, with arbitrum ARB $0.1891 falling 3.6% and starknet STRK $0.05656 dropping 3.2%. Starknet remains up about 29% over the month after surging on Oct. 9 and 10, when the network said it was considering becoming a standalone quantum-resistant layer-1 by 2027. DeFi tokens handed back more of Monday’s rally, with uniswap (UNI) losing 2.3% to about $7.14 and morpho MORPHO $2.4161 down 2.5%. UNI has slumped about 20% over the month even though its fee switch lifted protocol revenue to $14.81 million in September, its strongest month since it began retaining fees, according to Token Terminal. Ethena (ENA) fell 1.9%, extending a decline of about 30% over the month from a late-September peak near 29 cents. By  Omkar Godbole | Edited by  Sheldon Reback Updated  Oct 19, 2026, 10:06 a.m. EDT Published Oct 19, 2026, 6:03 a.m. EDT 2  min read Make preferred on Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email Make preferred on JPMorgan to bring JPM Coin to Ethereum. (Ikechukwu Julius Ugwu/Unsplash) Summary Show JPMorgan made JPM Coin, a token representing dollar deposits at the bank, available to institutional clients on Ethereum. Ethereum’s liquidity makes it attractive for crypto companies seeking blockchain payments and financial firms settling trades or backing tokenized assets, the bank told Bloomberg. The move expands JPMorgan’s blockchain efforts beyond its private Kinexys network, which processes more than $7 billion in transactions daily, and the Ethereum layer-2 network, Base. JPMorgan(JPM), the largest U.S. bank, brought its almost year-old crypto token , JPM Coin, to Ethereum as part of a plan to expand beyond Base, the layer-2 blockchain built by Coinbase Global COIN . JPM Coin , which represents dollar deposits at the bank, was technically deployed on the Ethereum mainnet on Monday and is available for institutional clients’ use, the bank said in an emailed statement. The bank chose Ethereum because the blockchain offers more liquidity than rival networks and is already used by institutional clients, Emma Landriault, the head of Kinexys Labs at JPMorgan’s blockchain division Kinexys, said in an interview with Bloomberg , which reported the news earlier. “Issuing JPM Coin first on Base and now on Ethereum is a meaningful step towards providing our institutional clients with multi-chain optionality for moving wholesale money across both the web3 and traditional finance ecosystems,” she said in the emailed statement. The banking giant flagged a move outside Base back in January, saying it was planning to take the token to the Canton Network. Broadening its availability aims to serve crypto firms that want to make blockchain payments and financial firms that need a digital token to settle trades or back tokenized assets, Landriault said. Tokenization is the process of converting real-world assets and financial assets into a digital form that’s recorded and traded on a decentralized ledger. The advantage is speed, including faster settlement of trades, quick movement of money while bypassing delays and frictions involved in traditional rails. Banks have embraced tokenization, but mostly away from public networks. In the U.S., JPMorgan, Citi (C), Bank of America (BAC) and Wells Fargo (WFC), along with more than a dozen other banks, have plans to start a shared network for tokenized deposits. JPMorgan’s private blockchain network, Kinexys, already handles more than $7 billion a day, a small piece in the bank’s $12 trillion a day payments business. Almost $50 billion worth of crypto assets are locked in Ethereum-based applications, according to DeFiLlama . Abroad, JPMorgan is among more than 30 banks that are helping Swift , the interbank messaging service, define the features and governance of its blockchain-based ledger. In July, Swift said 17 banks, including Citi and Wells Fargo, were preparing to pilot live transactions on it. JPMorgan wasn’t on that list. Weeks after bitcoin’s (BTC) price chart flashed a major bullish signal, Strategy MSTR , the largest publicly listed accumulator of the cryptocurrency, is about to do the same. The signal, a golden cross, occurs when a security’s 50-day average price rises above its 200-day average. Some traders read the transition as a decisive bullish shift in momentum that can lead to a prolonged rally. For MSTR, which holds $69.81 billion in bitcoin, the cross could happen as soon as Monday. Since the company began buying the largest cryptocurrency for its balance sheet in August 2020, the stock has had two such crosses, and huge rallies followed both. The first happened on Sept. 15, 2020, with the stock at about $15.57. MSTR climbed to $127.29 by February 2021, a gain of 717%. A death cross, the opposite of golden cross, followed in January 2022. By then, the stock was at $46.83, still triple the value on the day the bullish signal first appeared. The second came on March 2, 2023, at $25.29. The shares peaked at $473.83 in November 2024, up 1,774%. When the death cross arrived in October 2025, MSTR was at $328.40, still 1,199% higher. It’s worth keeping in mind that the signal isn’t especially reliable. In MSTR’s case, since 1999, the shares have registered 19 golden crosses. On 11 occasions, the stock was higher three months later, and after only 10 was it higher 12 months later, according to data analyzed by CoinDesk. That’s a record of 50% accuracy. The median 12-month return was just 3.3%, and the two worst crosses, in 2001 and 2007, were followed by a 61% loss. Since bitcoin confirmed its golden cross on Sept. 8, it has risen by nearly 5% to $82,000, extending the rally from July lows under $60,000. The price hit a high of over $87,000 early this month. By  Shaurya Malwa Oct 19, 2026, 12:54 a.m. EDT 2  min read Make preferred on Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email Make preferred on XRP Ledger is set to fix its lending code before anyone can use it. (Markus Spiske/Unsplash) Summary Show A package of XRP Ledger bug fixes is expected to take effect around 09:34 UTC on Oct. 23 after securing the minimum 29 validator votes required for approval. The fixes address Ripple’s proposed uncollateralized lending system, which remains inactive because its lending and vault amendments have only 19 and 21 votes, respectively. The package also closes a loophole that could allow certain accounts to create tokens despite having permission only to destroy them, while revising vault rounding and loan-default rules. A batch of bug fixes is set to go live on the XRP Ledger on Friday, and some of them patch the lending system Ripple has pitched to banks and payment companies since June — a system that hasn’t been switched on yet and is still 10 votes short of approval. Validators are the independent servers that agree on which transactions count. A change to the network’s rules needs backing from more than 80% of the 35 validators the network trusts by default, which works out to 29, and that backing has to hold for two straight weeks. Under the plan , a lender deposits XRP or another token into a vault, and a loan broker lends that money out for a fixed term. The ledger records the loan and tracks repayments, and the broker decides offchain whether a borrowe Borrowers don’t post collateral, so the broker’s judgment is all that stands between lenders and a default. Ripple has pitched the setup to payment companies that need cash while a cross-border settlement clears. The bug-fix package, called fixCleanup3_4_0, had exactly 29 votes as of Monday, according to the XRPL Dashboard . It’s nine days into its two-week countdown and on course to go live around 09:34 UTC on Oct. 23. It has no votes to spare, so one validator pulling support would restart the clock. The lending system has 19 votes. The vaults that would hold lenders’ money are a separate change and have 21. Neither has started a countdown, so even if both hit 29 votes today, lending couldn’t go live before early November. Separately, the patch also closes a loophole that could let an account allowed only to burn, or destroy, tokens on an issuer’s behalf create new ones under certain conditions, according to the xrpld 3.4.0 release notes . It will further changes how vaults round amounts and how the lending code decides when a loan is late or in default. It is one of several long-dormant wallets to wake up recently. By  Omkar Godbole Updated  Oct 19, 2026, 9:30 a.m. EDT Published Oct 19, 2026, 2:23 a.m. EDT 2  min read Make preferred on Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email Make preferred on Long-dormant BTC whale wakes up. (Arkham) Summary Show A Bitcoin wallet dormant since 2013 transferred all 411.45 of its coins, now worth about $34 million, to a new address on Sunday. The owner acquired most of the Bitcoin when it was worth about $54,000 and held it through major market swings as its value increased more than 600-fold. The funds have not moved to an exchange, and the transfer to a modern SegWit address suggests a security upgrade rather than an imminent sale. A bitcoin BTC $81,522.53 wallet, dormant since 2013, has come back to life. On Sunday, the wallet moved all 411.45 of its BTC to a new address, according to blockchain data from Arkham Intelligence. At today’s price of about $82,600 per coin, that stash is worth roughly $34 million. When the owner first acquired those coins, the entire balance was worth just $54,000. This awakening is part of a broader trend of historic supply shifting wallets this month. Just a day prior, two other wallets dormant for over a decade moved a combined 417 Bitcoin, and the week before, a large whale wallet static since the pre-Covid crash migrated its funds . The pattern is highly reminiscent of 2025, when isolated mega-whales repeatedly woke up from a prolonged slumber. Just like last year, these sudden movements of long-dormant supply tend to spark speculation about a potential sale. But, as was the case then, most of the coins have been moved to new private wallets, a sign of custodial maintenance rather than an impending market dump. The specific wallet behind Sunday's move received the bulk of its funds, some 411 BTC, on Sept. 11, 2013. Back then the cryptocurrency traded around $131. Over the next 13 years, the owner didn't buy, sell, or move a single coin. They simply sat tight as the asset's value skyrocketed more than 600 times, holding through three halvings, the 2017 boom, the 2022 FTX collapse, and the launch of spot bitcoin ETFs in 2024. While the owner remained completely inactive, the wallet itself did see some activity over the years. Dozens of tiny deposits trickled in, each worth less than a dollar. Several came from addresses that Arkham labels as phishing . It’s a common scam tactic known as “address poisoning.” Fraudsters send trace amounts of crypto ("dust") to high-value wallets, hoping the owner will accidentally copy the scammer's address from their transaction history during a future transfer. The whale didn't fall for it. At 18:23 UTC on Sunday, the owner sent the entire fortune to a new address, paying a transaction fee of just 337 satoshis, a fraction of a single cent. So far, the funds have not been moved to an exchange. The new destination wallet has only received this single transfer and has not initiated any outgoing transactions. That lack of movement points to routine custodial housekeeping rather than a market sell-off. (Helene Braun/CoinDesk) Summary Show Tether CEO Paulo Ardoino posted on X that his company is often way ahead of government sanctions when it freezes suspicious transactions — a point he contends a recent report from Senate Democrats ignored. He said he's confident Tether is "doing the right thing." Tether is answering back against a report issued last month by Democrats on the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations that had accused the stablecoin firm of providing "a significant financial lifeline within Iran's shadow banking network," with Tether CEO Paulo Ardoino saying Monday that the probe missed the positive work it's doing to observe sanctions. Senator Richard Blumenthal, the subcommittee's top Democrat, led the effort, which further highlighted Democratic lawmakers' concerns that crypto is used to support illicit finance. But Ardoino contends that Tether freezes suspicious transactions well before entities such as the U.S. Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control and Israel's National Bureau for Counter Terror Financing formally flag them. "Senator Blumenthal's 'analysis' of Tether's sanctions report misses that, since 2023, Tether froze on average 4 weeks prior to OFAC & NBCTF official sanction designation and for 99% of the times Tether froze the reported addresses before Chainalysis labelled them," Ardoino wrote in a post on social media site X . Ardoino went on to argue that the company's actions "led to Iran-linked stablecoin volumes declining by 94%." Tether's CEO also spoke remotely at a Washington event, DC Fintech Week, and addressed the senator's report there, as well, last Tuesday. He criticized how it was released to the media before his company could review it. "I believe it's important for the public also to hear our side of the story," he said. "Our aim is to push out the bad actors from USDT," Ardoino said. "Those bad actors are moving to other means that are outside of the control of the United States, and now outside of our control." He added that the work "is not finished," but he said he's happy with Tether's role. "I wake up in the morning and I look at myself in the mirror, and I know that we're doing the right thing," he said. The Senate report went back a number of years, focusing in part on the period before 2024 in which it said Tether didn't comprehensively freeze flagged wallets. "This absence of deterrence invited abuse: Terrorist organizations such as Hamas shifted from transacting in bitcoin and a mix of cryptocurrencies to promoting USDT," it said. Since the report, Blumenthal has additionally been probing the relationship between Tether and its U.S. financial partner, Cantor Fitzgerald, which has close ties to the administration of President Donald Trump. Tether also named Bo Hines, Trump's former White House crypto adviser, as the CEO of its U.S. division last fall. Overview Ethena is a synthetic dollar protocol built on crypto rails, issuing USDe - a dollar-denominated digital asset - alongside sUSDe, the protocol's autonomously and permissionlessly created globally accessible savings asset. USDe is designed around four principles that together define a superior product for holders of digital dollars: Capital efficiency Industry leading ecosystem rewards Resilience across market cycles Infrastructure to capture every available source of dollar returns within reserve assets Capital efficiency Each unit of USDe is backed by assets held by the protocol. Virtually every dollar of backing remains productive, generating revenue through the strategies described below, and USDe scales without the onerous collateral buffers required by other decentralised stablecoin designs. Capital efficiency at the protocol level translates directly into rewards available to the ecosystem. Industry-leading ecosystem rewards Revenue earned on the backing of USDe is utilized in promotional and incentive programs, including sUSDe (which is maintained by a subsidiary of the Ethena Foundation)and certain partner reward programs on partner exchanges, platforms, or protocols. That revenue is generated from a diversified set of strategies, including: Funding rates on delta-neutral basis trades in crypto perpetual and futures markets; Funding rates on delta-neutral basis trades in non-crypto markets; Lending revenue from overcollateralised on-chain DeFi lending markets; Lending revenue from overcollateralised loans to institutional counterparties; Rewards on tokenised real-world assets, including short-duration government debt and high-liquidity credit; Rewards on liquid stablecoin holdings where applicable. Resilience across market cycles Each strategy responds to a different driver. Crypto funding rates reflect leverage demand in digital asset markets. Non-crypto funding rates reflect demand for leverage in commodities and other markets. Lending revenue reflects borrowing demand in DeFi and at institutional venues. Real-world asset returns reflect rates in traditional fixed income. These drivers are largely uncorrelated, which means weakness in any one source can be offset by strength in others. That diversification across revenue sources mitigates risk across the entire protocol. The backing portfolio is also dynamic. The protocol can shift weight between strategies as conditions evolve, subject to governance and Risk Committee review. In periods when crypto funding rates compress, the portfolio can lean into lending, real-world assets, and non-crypto basis to mitigate associated risks while being revenue positive. When leverage demand in crypto markets accelerates and perpetual funding rises, the portfolio can shift weight back towards crypto basis trades to capture that opportunity at scale - the only protocol in the industry that has the infrastructure set up to do so. Positioned to capture every available source of dollar returns Accessing this full set of strategies requires infrastructure that few protocols possess: off-exchange custody with multiple regulated providers, direct relationships with the deepest crypto and commodity derivatives venues, onboarded counterparties for institutional lending, integrations with leading tokenised real-world asset issuers, and exposure into curated DeFi lending markets - all governed by a Risk Committee setting consistent exposure limits across categories. Ethena has built this infrastructure since launch and is operating it at the scale required to make each category of backing materially additive to USDe’s resilience and profile.
